chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from a man, from Ja'far ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Pleasure (or delight) is in ten things: walking, riding, swimming in water, looking at greenery, eating and drinking, looking at a beautiful woman, sexual intercourse, using the siwak (tooth-stick), and conversing with men.

key_terms.السِّوَاكُ: Using a tooth-stick for oral hygiene
key_terms.الْإِرْتِمَاسُ: Swimming or immersing oneself in water

ai.seo_question: What are the ten things that bring pleasure according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies ten sources of *al-nashwah* (delight or pleasure), categorizing them into physical, sensory, and social domains. This enumeration reflects the Shia theological view that bodily pleasures are not merely distractions but inherent aspects of human nature (*fitrah*) that, when enjoyed within proper bounds, contribute to spiritual well-being and gratitude.
